_comment: The gate contract for Kestrel's canon. cb.py gates reads this file; no threshold lives in the skill or the code. Every gate carries its reason and its baseline. Rule of entry: if a number cannot turn red, it does not belong in `metrics`; put it in `tira` (the strip) instead. numerador/denominador are dotted paths into `cb.py stats --json`.

metrics.que_mide: Share of lifecycle notes (canon + tech) that a person has validated
metrics.por_que: Below half, retrieve serves more unverified notes than verified ones, and people stop trusting the badge. 0.5 is where Maya stopped reading the validated label during the September review.

metrics.que_mide: Lifecycle notes past expires_on that nobody revalidated
metrics.por_que: validate drains about 3 notes a week. More than 3 expired means the queue is losing, not that the canon is old. One is normal churn.

metrics.que_mide: Notes whose source has a dated entry in extraction-log that actually carry occurred_on
metrics.por_que: Only recoverable notes are measured: a hand-captured note with no dated source cannot have occurred_on, and gating it would be noise. If the date is sitting in the log and the note lacks it, that is a one-command fix (cb.py dates --write), so anything below 95 % is laziness, below 80 % is broken extraction.

metrics.que_mide: Markdown files inside Context/ with no contract type
metrics.por_que: A file in Context/ without a type shows up in every grep as if it were canon, with no owner, no expiry and no validation. Zero tolerance: give it frontmatter or move it out.

metrics.que_mide: Open bets whose deadline has passed
metrics.por_que: A bet nobody closes is a prediction that risks nothing. One overdue bet is a busy week; three means the mechanism is decorative.

metrics.que_mide: Human graph edges that say who declared them and how
metrics.por_que: An edge without declared_via cannot be told apart from an invented one, and gets served with the same authority. There is no acceptable share of unattributed edges.

metrics.que_mide: Retrieval-log entries that record which notes were actually used
metrics.por_que: notas_usadas is the only gold set this canon will ever have for measuring recall. An entry that returns nothing useful is legitimate (it should have a gap instead), so 100 % is not the target; under half means people stopped filling it in.
Without session_id there is no leave-one-session-out, and any signal tuned on the log gets evaluated on itself.

tira.que_mide: Lifecycle notes with 2+ search_terms that resolve against ontology.json
tira.por_que_sin_gate: We do not know what good looks like yet; a gate invented today is a gate nobody audits.

tira.que_mide: Median days between the event and its capture
tira.por_que_sin_gate: Exposure of the captured_on clock policy. Watched, not gated: the policy was chosen knowingly.

tira.que_mide: Live notes whose event already fell outside its type's validity window
tira.por_que_sin_gate: Same as above: the visible cost of anchoring expiry on capture, not a defect.

tira.que_mide: Decision-logs that declare what they supersede
tira.por_que_sin_gate: Most decisions supersede nothing. The useful number is candidates left unjudged (cb.py supersession), which stats does not export yet.

tira.que_mide: Lifecycle notes expiring in the next 30 days
tira.por_que_sin_gate: Next month's validate workload. Planning input, not a health signal.
